text: The public API `parseUrl(url, normalize)` (entry point, src/index.js:35) takes `url` as fully attacker-controlled input. Graph-confirmed FLOWS_TO chain: normalizeUrl(url, normalize) [line 60] -> parsePath(url) [line 63] -> parsed.href.match(GIT_RE) [line 67], where GIT_RE is a hand-rolled multi-group regex `/(^(git@|http(s)?:\/\/)([\w\.\-@]+)(\/|:))(([\~,\.\w,\-,\_,\/]+)(.git){0,1}((\/){0,1}))/`. The only mitigation is a length cap (parseUrl.MAX_INPUT_LENGTH = 2048) applied earlier in the function; up to 2048 bytes of raw attacker-supplied text is still run through this regex with no further sanitization when parsePath reports parse_failed. This is the exact GIT_RE pattern historically associated with ReDoS reports in the parse-url package family. No other dangerous sink (exec/sql/redirect/code_exec) exists anywhere in this 2-file repo, so this regex-match is the only non-trivial sink reachable from attacker input.
